source: Khajah, Lindsey, Mozer (2016) How deep is knowledge tracing?
finding: Part of DKT's reported lead over Bayesian knowledge tracing (BKT) came from a biased AUC procedure used for BKT.
numbers: 31.6% of the DKT-BKT gap reported by Piech et al. traced to biased AUC computation for BKT. Replicated BKT scored 0.73 vs 0.67 reported (ASSISTments) and 0.62 vs 0.54 (synthetic).
limits: Authors cannot be sure what Piech et al. did; they infer it.
agent_relevance: Check the baseline was scored the same way as the new model before believing a big gain.

source: Khajah, Lindsey, Mozer (2016) How deep is knowledge tracing?
finding: Adding forgetting to BKT removed about half of the remaining gap on ASSISTments.
numbers: Another 50.6% of the gap vanished when BKT got forgetting. BKT+F on ASSISTments about 0.83 AUC; DKT reported 0.86.
limits: Gap not fully closed on ASSISTments: enhanced BKT trails DKT by 8.3% (0.03 AUC).
agent_relevance: Simple, interpretable state models with the right terms (recency, forgetting) match deep nets; a scaffold can keep explicit learner or task state.

source: Khajah, Lindsey, Mozer (2016) How deep is knowledge tracing?
finding: Across four datasets, extended BKT (forgetting, student ability, skill discovery) is on average indistinguishable from DKT.
numbers: Enhanced BKT beat DKT by 20.0% (0.05 AUC) on Synthetic and 3.0% on Spanish; lost by 8.3% on ASSISTments and 3.5% on Statics. Statics: BKT+FSA 0.75 vs DKT 0.76. Spanish (182 students, 409 exercises): 0.846 vs 0.836.
quote: DKT's success is flexibility and generality in capturing statistical regularities directly present in the inputs
limits: Four datasets only. Skill labels hurt BKT: Statics 0.73 with skill labels vs 0.81 with exercise-indexed labels in another study.
agent_relevance: DKT's edge is flexibility to capture regularities, not representation discovery.

source: Wilson, Karklin, Han, Ekanadham (2016) Back to the basics: Bayesian extensions of IRT outperform neural networks
finding: Item response theory (IRT) models matched or beat DKT on three datasets (ASSISTments, KDD Cup Bridge to Algebra 2006-07, Knewton proprietary).
numbers: Hierarchical IRT best overall. ASSISTments after cleaning: 346,740 interactions, 4,097 users, 26,684 items. KDD: 3,679,198 interactions, 1,146 users. DKT could not be tuned to tens of thousands of items.
limits: Exact AUC per model read only from a garbled figure; direction is clear, digits not recorded.
agent_relevance: Strong static baselines (difficulty plus ability) are hard to beat; test them first.

source: Wilson, Karklin, Han, Ekanadham (2016) Back to the basics: Bayesian extensions of IRT outperform neural networks
finding: DKT's 0.86 AUC on ASSISTments was reproduced only when duplicate rows were left in; removing them negated the gain.
numbers: Duplicate rows were about 25% of ASSISTments rows and leak the ground truth in online prediction. Their RNN reproduced 0.86 on raw data.
limits: Per-skill BKT is not exposed to this leak because it splits data by skill.
agent_relevance: Data leakage can fake a large effect; check for duplicate or repeated rows in any tracing eval.

source: Wilson, Karklin, Han, Ekanadham (2016) Back to the basics: Bayesian extensions of IRT outperform neural networks
finding: Temporal IRT helped only where the data had real sequence structure (Knewton data).
numbers: On Knewton an optimal window length existed; on ASSISTments and KDD longer windows were as good, so static models sufficed.
limits: DKT lagged even where temporal structure existed; authors do not explain why.
agent_relevance: Check whether order matters in the data before paying for a sequence model.

source: Liu et al. (2022) pyKT: benchmark of deep learning knowledge tracing
finding: Standardised benchmark of 10 deep KT models on 7 datasets. Most newer models do not clearly beat the original DKT.
numbers: 5-fold CV. AKT best nearly everywhere: +3.06% AS2009, +1.50% AL2005, +1.62% BD2006, +1.60% NIPS34 over second best; only +0.30% Statics2011 and +1.08% POJ.
limits: Single library and its preprocessing; authors call improvements minimal vs DKT.
agent_relevance: Progress claims in this field shrink under common evaluation.

source: Liu et al. (2022) pyKT: benchmark of deep learning knowledge tracing
finding: Label leakage from expanding each question into several concept steps inflates AUC.
numbers: Mean leaked gain 8.38% (AS2009) and 13.09% (AL2005); about 0.1% on BD2006 and NIPS34 (about 1.01 concepts per question vs 1.20 and 1.36). DKT AS2009 leaked AUC 0.8262, gain 0.0843.
limits: Leakage matters only when questions have several concepts.
agent_relevance: Leakage explains failures to reproduce many published models on AS2009 and AL2005.

source: Liu et al. (2022) pyKT: benchmark of deep learning knowledge tracing
finding: ATKT's published results could not be reproduced once its use of future ground truth was fixed.
numbers: Original code used future labels to predict current mastery; fixed results were lower.
limits: Detail in appendix A.5, not read.
agent_relevance: Check for hidden future information in any learner-tracing loop.

source: Liu et al. (2022) pyKT: benchmark of deep learning knowledge tracing
finding: Self-attention KT models (SAKT, SAINT) often lose to recurrent DKT; programming exercises are much harder to predict.
numbers: Math AUC about 0.8; POJ programming about 0.6.
limits: Authors give a recency/forgetting explanation, not tested here.
agent_relevance: Far history matters little for next-step correctness; recent evidence dominates.

source: Piech et al. (2015) Deep Knowledge Tracing
finding: Founding DKT paper: an RNN/LSTM predicts next-answer correctness without hand-coded skills.
numbers: AUC: Khan Academy 0.85 vs BKT 0.68 (marginal baseline 0.63); ASSISTments 0.86 vs 0.69 best prior (called a 25% gain). Khan data 1.4 million exercises.
limits: Later work shows the ASSISTments gain was inflated by duplicate rows and a biased BKT AUC (b02, b05).
agent_relevance: Origin of the claim that sequence models need no explicit skill structure; weakened by replications.

source: Ghosh, Heffernan, Lan (2020) Context-aware attentive knowledge tracing (AKT)
finding: AKT adds Rasch-style question embeddings and monotonic attention (decay with distance).
numbers: Up to 6% AUC over baselines. Without question IDs: +6% ASSISTments2015, +1% ASSISTments2017, on par on Statics2011 and ASSISTments2009. With IDs: +2% (2009), +6% (2017). Authors found DKT beat DKVMN in their re-run.
limits: Authors re-implemented baselines; pyKT later found smaller margins.
agent_relevance: Item difficulty terms from psychometrics add more than deeper sequence machinery.

source: Kestin et al. (2025) AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning, Scientific Reports
finding: Randomised crossover trial at Harvard (physics, N=194): a custom LLM tutor beat in-class active learning.
numbers: Median post-score 4.5 (AI, N=142) vs 3.5 (active class, N=174); pre-test 2.75. Effect size 0.63 by regression, 0.73 to 1.3 SD by quantile regression (p<1e-8). Median time 49 min vs about 60.
limits: One course, one topic pair, short lesson, immediate post-test; tutor prompt carried expert step-by-step solutions and pedagogy rules.
agent_relevance: Prompts with explicit expert solutions and pedagogy rules work; a scaffold with explicit guidance can help.

source: Kestin et al. (2025) AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning, Scientific Reports
finding: Time on task did not predict post-test score; students felt more engaged and motivated with the AI tutor.
numbers: No correlation between time on task and post-test; 70% of AI group spent under 60 min.
limits: Self-reported engagement; no delayed test.
agent_relevance: Efficiency gain is real in this setting but retention is untested.

source: Pardos, Bhandari (2023) Learning gain differences between ChatGPT and human tutor generated algebra hints
finding: Early ChatGPT hints were worse than human-written hints for learning gain.
numbers: 77 MTurk participants, 2x2: Elementary Algebra control 19 / ChatGPT 21; Intermediate control 17 / ChatGPT 20. 70% of ChatGPT hints passed manual quality check. Pre-post gain significant only for human hints (p=0.0219, p=0.0213); ChatGPT p=0.1427, 0.7912. Human > ChatGPT gain, p=0.038.
limits: Small N; MTurk adults; ChatGPT group near ceiling at pre-test in Intermediate (80.05% vs 50.94%); human hints requested more (132 vs 30; 150 vs 57), a confound.
agent_relevance: Hint quality filtering was needed; unfiltered LLM output cannot be trusted as tutoring.

source: Wang, Ribeiro, Robinson, Loeb, Demszky (2024) Tutor CoPilot
finding: Preregistered RCT in real tutoring: LLM suggestions to human tutors raised mastery.
numbers: Students were 4 percentage points more likely to pass exit tickets (p<.01); 9 points for students of lower-rated tutors. Cost about $20 per tutor per year. Over 350,000 messages analysed; 900 tutors initially identified.
limits: Outcome is topic mastery per session, not a long-term test; AI assists a human, not alone.
agent_relevance: Gains concentrate where the human is weakest; a scaffold helps most on weak base ability.

source: Language model-based Knowledge Tracing, LKT (2024)
finding: Pretrained language models on question text roughly tie DKT on a large dataset and lose on a small one.
numbers: XES3G5M-T AUC: best LKT ERNIE-2.0 0.8508 vs DKT 0.8480, DKVMN 0.8513 (no clear win). DBE-KT22: AKT 0.7984 vs best LKT 0.7643.
limits: Margins within about one standard deviation on XES3G5M-T; DKT numbers partly taken from another paper.
agent_relevance: Text helps cold start and transfer, not raw accuracy.

source: Language model-based Knowledge Tracing, LKT (2024)
finding: LKT pretrained on one dataset works zero-shot on another, where DKT cannot.
numbers: DKT scored 0.5 AUC with no target data because it needs ids; LKT pretrained on DBE-KT22 beat DKT on small XES3G5M-T slices.
limits: Claim from figures; exact values not read.
agent_relevance: Text-based state tracing generalises to new content without retraining.

source: Scarlatos et al. (2024) Exploring knowledge tracing in tutor-student dialogues using LLMs
finding: A fine-tuned LLM (LLMKT) beats classic KT on open dialogue, where classic methods fail.
numbers: CoMTA (small): all classic KT near chance (majority class Acc 57.83, AUC 50). LLMKT AUC 61.82 vs DKT 52.50, DKT-Sem 51.25. MathDial AUC: LLMKT 66.18 vs DKT 64.19, SAINT 63.31.
limits: Std on CoMTA large (about 6 AUC points); labels from GPT-4o; over 90% of CoMTA labels are correct answers.
agent_relevance: Direct test of tracing what a learner knows from free text; relevant for tracking a user or sub-agent state.

source: Scarlatos et al. (2024) Exploring knowledge tracing in tutor-student dialogues using LLMs
finding: GPT-4o labelling of correctness and concepts is near human level but noisy.
numbers: Final-turn correctness accuracy about 78 on CoMTA, annotators only slightly higher. Kappa low on correctness (class imbalance), moderate on concepts. Only 5 of 15 frequent concepts trended to higher mastery.
limits: Human evaluation small.
agent_relevance: LLM judges of learner state have error; report it.

source: Sonkar et al. (2023) CLASS framework for LLM tutors
finding: Builds a tutor from Vicuna-13B using GPT-4-generated simulated tutoring and scaffolding dialogues.
numbers: Training data synthetic from GPT-4; base model Vicuna-13B.
limits: Only skimmed; no learning outcome measured in the parts read.
agent_relevance: Shows synthetic dialogue data is used, but gives no outcome evidence.

source: Corbett, Anderson (1995) Knowledge tracing: modeling the acquisition of procedural knowledge
finding: Original BKT with four parameters (prior, learn, guess, slip) and mastery learning in the ACT-R LISP tutor.
numbers: Mastery threshold 0.95 (recalled, not checked).
limits: Not opened; recalled from memory.
agent_relevance: The base model of this subfield.

source: Beck, Chang (2007); Doroudi, Brunskill (2017) identifiability of BKT
finding: BKT parameters are not uniquely identified; different fits give similar predictions but different mastery decisions.
numbers: Not checked this session.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Learner-state estimates can be wrong while predictions look fine.

source: Pane et al. (2014) RAND Cognitive Tutor Algebra I
finding: Large randomised trial of Cognitive Tutor Algebra I: no clear effect in year one, positive in year two.
numbers: Recalled: about 147 schools, about 0.20 SD in year two for high school. Unverified.
limits: Not opened; RAND fetch gave HTTP 403.
agent_relevance: Even well-built tutors may take a year to show gains.

source: VanLehn (2011) Relative effectiveness of human tutoring, ITS and other tutoring systems
finding: Step-based tutors near human tutors; answer-based tutors much lower.
numbers: Recalled: d about 0.76 step-based, 0.79 human, 0.31 answer-based. Unverified.
limits: Not opened; fetch failed.
agent_relevance: Granularity of feedback matters more than who gives it.

source: Kulik, Fletcher (2016) Effectiveness of intelligent tutoring systems: meta-analytic review
finding: ITS raised test scores over conventional instruction.
numbers: Recalled: 50 studies, median effect about 0.66, smaller on standardised tests. Unverified.
limits: Not opened; search budget exhausted.
agent_relevance: Effect sizes shrink with standardised outcomes.

source: Bastani et al. (2025) Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning, PNAS
finding: Unrestricted GPT help improved practice but hurt later exam performance; a guarded tutor version removed the harm.
numbers: Recalled: about 1,000 high-school students; GPT Base about +48% practice, about -17% exam. Unverified.
limits: Not opened; fetch returned HTTP 403.
agent_relevance: Guardrails on tutoring behaviour are essential; matches our guardrail idea.

source: Schwonke et al. (2009) Cognitive Tutor Algebra with worked examples
finding: Adding faded worked examples to Cognitive Tutor gave equal learning in less time.
numbers: Not checked this session.
